newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate dips on pre-weekend demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate dips on pre-weekend demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened 20 basis points lower at 18.55 percent on Wednesday due to demand for paper ahead of the forthcoming long weekend in Mexico, traders said.
"Many are covering shorts and that is why rates are down a little," a trader said.
Mexico celebrates public holidays on Thursday, May 1, for Labor Day and Battle of Puebla day on Monday, May 5.
"Many are trading at six days, until next Tuesday, so most will be covering shorts today, rather than Friday," another trader said.
"Investors rushed to pick up paper at the open, without them being bothered that rates are a little low," an analyst added.

Analysts had originally foreseen some upside pressure on rates due to early gains in U.S. long bond yields, but said this was no longer likely as the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was now up 17/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper opened up five basis points at 19.05 percent.

Liquidity of 6.342 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation, with a further 1.8 billion pesos entering the system from an underplacement carried over from the primary auction on Monday.
Nonetheless, traders expected outflows of some 7.5 billion pesos in month-end demand for cash and to pay corporate tax bills.
